subject: physics
question_text: What are the SI unit and the dimensional formula of stress?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya *IPE Study Material for Jr. Students* 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 9 Very Short Answer Question 6 (printed p.98). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: SI unit of stress is N/m² (pascal); dimensional formula is [M¹L⁻¹T⁻²], obtained by dividing force's dimensions [M¹L¹T⁻²] by area's dimensions [L²].

insider_note: Examiners award one mark for the unit and one for the dimensional formula, so giving only one of the two, even correctly, costs a mark.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: SI unit of stress
lines: Stress = force / area, so its unit is the
unit of force divided by the unit of area.

lines.text: SI unit of stress = N/m² (pascal, Pa)

steps.margin_note: Name the unit AND its symbol N/m² — a bare 'pascal' without the symbol form loses this mark.
steps.why: The unit of a quotient is the quotient of the units, so newton (force) over square metre (area) gives the unit of stress directly.
common_mistakes: Writing N/m instead of N/m² — area is squared.
Forgetting the alternate name pascal (Pa) for the SI unit.
steps.memory_tip: Stress shares its unit with pressure: N per square metre, also called the pascal.

steps.label: Dimensional formula
lines: Force has dimensions [M¹L¹T⁻²] and area has
steps.margin_note: Both the SI unit and the dimensional formula must appear — one alone is half the answer.
steps.why: Stress equals force divided by area, and substituting the dimensional formulas of force [M¹L¹T⁻²] and area [L²] gives the dimensional formula of stress directly.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the negative sign in the exponent of L or T.
Confusing stress's dimensions with strain, which has none.
steps.memory_tip: Divide force's [M¹L¹T⁻²] by area's [L²]: the L power drops from 1 to −1.
